_comment: The signing keys this build of Agentry Desktop trusts for 'a newer Agentry
Desktop'. The release
workflow signs SHA256SUMS with the private half of one of these; the app
and the site's downloads importer verify against the public halves here.
This is OUR key, not the operating system's: it is independent of Developer
ID signing and Authenticode, which secure a
different thing.
Fields, per key:
name       what this key is called in the record and in error messages
('dev', 'prod'). Stable; a key keeps its name forever.
publicKey  the bare minisign public-key line — the second line of a
minisign .pub file, and exactly what `minisign -P` accepts,
so shell and Go read the same string.
keyID      the 16 hex digits minisign prints for this key. Redundant with
publicKey on purpose: the loader derives the id and refuses a
file where the two disagree, which catches a paste that took
the comment line from one key and the base64 from another.
retired    true once a newer key has taken over. A retired key still
VERIFIES — that is the point of keeping it, so an old release
stays checkable — but callers refuse to install from one.
addedAt    the day it was added, ISO date. For the record only.
note       where the private half lives and what it is for: every
repository that holds it, since the CLI and the MCP server
sign with the same key.
proof      the key's own signature over a statement naming this file,
the entry's name, its key id and its public key: evidence
that whoever added the key holds its private half. A current
key needs one; at most one key is current.
endorsement the signature of the key recorded just before this one
over the hand-over to this entry: evidence that whoever
held the outgoing key agreed to the rotation. Every key but
dev and prod, the two recorded before endorsements, needs
one, so the chain runs unbroken to the current key.
A build with no keys here trusts nothing and refuses every update; that is
the correct state for the open core, which anyone can build.
Keys are added by `keyset add`, through operator/rotate-update-key.sh,
never by hand: the tools refuse a current key without its proof, a key
the key before it did not endorse, and a second current key, and the
wizard is what keeps the committed public
half and the Actions secret the two halves of one pair.

keys.name: dev
keys.note: private half: the AGENTRY_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY secret of blaktron/agentry-desktop. The CLI (a repository secret) and the MCP server (a secret of its release environment) sign with the same key under the same name; a rotation moves all three, with the DESKTOP_SIGNRELEASE_REF pins in their release workflows.

keys.name: prod
keys.note: production key; private half in the release environment of blaktron/agentry-release and the operator's password-protected backup
